title: Care Academy Q&A: Withdrawing a Delivery Claim
content:
**Rule.** Withdrawing a Delivery Claims claim is the customer's own decision and is possible only before a decision, while the claim is opened or in carrier trace. A claim is withdrawn only on the customer's own confirmation. A withdrawn claim does not count toward the repeat limit and frees the order for a new claim of the same type within the reporting window.

**Who decides that a claim is withdrawn?**
The customer. A claim is withdrawn only on the customer's own confirmation, never on the agent's initiative.

**In which statuses can a claim be withdrawn?**

| Claim status | Withdrawal possible |
|---|---|
| opened | yes |
| carrier trace | yes |
| under review, approved, denied, resolved | no — withdrawal is possible only while the claim is opened or in carrier trace |

**Does a withdrawn claim count toward the repeat limit?**
No. A withdrawn claim never counts toward the repeat limit.

**After a withdrawal, can the customer claim again on the same order?**
Yes, for a claim of the same type, provided the new claim is opened within the reporting window. The withdrawn claim no longer occupies the order's one claim of that type.

**Hypothetical case.** A customer's Delivered Not Received Claim is in carrier trace when the parcel turns up at a neighbour's. The customer confirms the withdrawal; the claim is withdrawn, it does not count toward the repeat limit, and the order is free for a new Delivered Not Received Claim within the reporting window if one is needed.
